items.title: Big agriculture mislead the public about the benefits of biofuels
items.title_zh: 大农业如何误导公众相信生物燃料的益处
items.summary: The article describes how lawyer Tim Searchinger, who lacked credentials as a scientist or economist, sensed something was wrong while reading about biofuels in spring 2003, and explores how big agriculture misled the public about their benefits.

items.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Agent casually clicks through "I am not a robot" verification
items.title_zh: OpenAI 的 ChatGPT Agent 轻松通过“我不是机器人”验证
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that OpenAI's ChatGPT agent passed an anti-bot screening step while stating that the step was needed to prove it was not a bot.

items.title: Attention is your scarcest resource (2020)
items.title_zh: 注意力是你最稀缺的资源（2020）
items.summary: A 2020 essay argues that attention is a scarce resource and offers practices such as monotasking, avoiding obligations, and timeboxing.

items.title: Programmers aren’t so humble anymore, maybe because nobody codes in Perl
items.title_zh: 程序员不再那么谦逊了，也许因为没人再用 Perl 编程
items.summary: A Wired piece describes Perl as a messy, maddening language — the “duct tape of the internet” — but one that was visibly made by humans, and reflects on changing programmer humility.

items.title: Show HN: Mcp-use – Connect any LLM to any MCP
items.title_zh: Show HN：mcp-use，把任意 LLM 连接到任意 MCP
items.summary: The authors of mcp-use built a high-level abstraction over the official MCP SDK that lets developers connect any LLM to any MCP server in six lines of code. They say it supports all protocol functionality and was created because MCP was initially usable only through applications such as Claude Desktop or Cursor.

items.title: FBI seized $40k from Linda Martin without charging her with a crime

items.summary: The article examines civil forfeiture, which allows law enforcement to seize assets without charging the owner with a crime, and argues there is little accountability in the practice.

items.title: I tried to replace myself with ChatGPT in my English class

items.summary: An English teacher recounts how students nicknamed ChatGPT “Chat” and use it to make study guides, interpret essay prompts and register for classes, as he tried replacing himself with the tool in his classroom.

items.summary: Anthropic said it will add weekly usage limits for Claude subscribers on August 28 alongside the existing five-hour limits, citing account sharing, reselling access, and around-the-clock background use; it estimated the change affects fewer than 5% of users.

items.title: A Transparent Fairness Evaluation Protocol for Open-Source Language Model Benchmarking on the Blockchain
items.title_zh: 面向区块链上开源语言模型基准测试的透明公平性评估协议
items.summary: The paper proposes a transparent fairness evaluation protocol for open-source LLMs that uses smart contracts on the Internet Computer Protocol blockchain to store datasets, prompts and metrics on-chain. It benchmarks Llama, DeepSeek and Mistral on the PISA dataset, adds StereoSet-derived bias metrics, and extends the analysis to English, Spanish and Portuguese.

items.title: CHECK-MAT: Checking Hand-Written Mathematical Answers for the Russian Unified State Exam
items.title_zh: CHECK-MAT：批改俄罗斯统一国家考试手写数学答案
items.summary: The paper introduces the EGE-Math Solutions Assessment Benchmark for evaluating vision-language models on grading scanned hand-written math solutions. It uses 122 solutions from the Russian Unified State Exam with official expert grades and tests seven VLMs from Google, OpenAI, Arcee AI and Alibaba Cloud in three inference modes.

items.title: Canoe Paddling Quality Assessment Using Smart Devices: Preliminary Machine Learning Study
items.title_zh: 基于智能设备的皮划艇划桨质量评估：初步机器学习研究
items.summary: The study presents an AI coaching system that trains machine learning models on motion data from Apple Watches and smartphones and delivers stroke feedback through an LLM; across four participants and 66 stroke samples, an Extremely Randomized Trees model reached an F score of 0.9496 under five-fold cross validation.

items.title: A Contrastive Diffusion-based Network (CDNet) for Time Series Classification
items.title_zh: CDNet：面向时间序列分类的对比扩散网络
items.summary: CDNet is a contrastive diffusion-based network that generates positive and negative samples through a learned diffusion process to improve time-series classifiers, particularly under noisy, similar, and multimodal conditions; experiments used the UCR Archive and simulated datasets.

items.title: SmartCLIP: Modular Vision-language Alignment with Identification Guarantees
items.title_zh: SmartCLIP：具备可识别性保证的模块化视觉-语言对齐
items.summary: The paper establishes theoretical conditions for aligning visual and textual representations at varying levels of granularity while preserving cross-modal semantics and disentangling visual features. It introduces SmartCLIP, a modular method that identifies and aligns the most relevant representations, with code released on GitHub.

items.title: To Theoretically Understand Transformer-Based In-Context Learning for Optimizing CSMA
items.title_zh: 从理论上理解基于 Transformer 的上下文学习如何优化 CSMA
items.summary: The paper proposes a transformer-based in-context learning optimizer that predicts contention window thresholds for CSMA channel access. NS-3 experiments show fast convergence and near-optimal throughput under unknown node densities compared with model-based and DRL-based approaches.

items.title: FlashSVD: Memory-Efficient Inference with Streaming for Low-Rank Models
items.title_zh: FlashSVD：面向低秩模型的内存高效流式推理
items.summary: FlashSVD is a rank-aware streaming inference framework for SVD-compressed LLMs that fuses low-rank projection kernels into self-attention and feed-forward pipelines; on standard encoder benchmarks such as BERT-Base it cuts peak activation memory by up to 70.2% and intermediate transient memory by 75% without accuracy loss.

items.title: Word Overuse and Alignment in Large Language Models: The Influence of Learning from Human Feedback
items.title_zh: 大语言模型中的词汇过度使用与对齐：人类反馈学习的影响
items.summary: Using Meta’s Llama, the study examines how learning from human feedback, which it treats as covering RLHF and direct preference optimization, contributes to LLM overuse of words such as “delve” and “intricate”. An experiment emulating the procedure found participants systematically preferred text variants containing certain words, which the authors frame as a kind of misalignment and a divergence between the expectations of feedback workers and model users.
